questions.question: Determine the power dissipated in the 100 ohm resistor.
questions.answer: Power = 2.7 x 10^-2 W
steps: The 100 ohm resistor has the voltmeter p.d. of 1.64 V across it.

questions.question: Discuss the student's prediction (shown in a missing image), without calculations.
questions.answer: The prediction is correct: the voltmeter reading would increase.
steps: After swapping, the parallel section is X (about 300 ohm) with 200 ohm, whose resistance (about 120 ohm) is greater than the original parallel section of X with 100 ohm (about 75 ohm).
The series resistor changes from 200 ohm to 100 ohm, so it is smaller.

In a potential divider, the section with the larger share of the total resistance has the larger share of the 6.00 V, so the p.d. across the parallel section, which is the voltmeter reading, rises (to about 3.3 V compared with 1.64 V).

questions.question: An NTC thermistor is connected in a circuit and its temperature is increased. Which row of the table gives the changes to the ammeter and voltmeter?
questions.answer: D: ammeter reading increases; voltmeter reading decreases
steps: Raising the temperature of an NTC thermistor lowers its resistance, so the total resistance falls and the current (ammeter) increases.
The p.d. across the fixed resistor (V = I R) rises, so the p.d. across the thermistor (voltmeter) = E - I R decreases. This is row D.

questions.question: Explain why mercury atoms emit photons after electrons collide with them in a UV lamp.
questions.answer: Collisions excite the mercury atoms to higher energy levels; when the electrons fall back they emit photons of UV frequency.
steps: Colliding electrons transfer kinetic energy to mercury atoms.
Electrons in the atoms are excited to higher energy levels.
When they fall back to lower levels, they emit photons with energy equal to the level difference (E = hf).

questions.question: UV intensity on the screen is 50 mW cm^-2 and the glue takes 25 s to harden. Show that the total energy incident on the glass screen is 130 J.
questions.answer: E = 131 J, which is about 130 J
steps: Screen area A = 7.15 cm x 14.7 cm = 105 cm^2.
Power on the screen P = intensity x area = 50 mW cm^-2 x 105 cm^2 = 5250 mW = 5.25 W.
Energy E = P t = 5.25 W x 25 s = 131 J, which is about 130 J.

questions.topic: Number of UV Photons on Screen
questions.question: With total energy 130 J of UV light at wavelength 395 nm, determine the number of photons incident on the glass screen.
questions.answer: N = 2.6 x 10^20 photons
steps: Number of photons N = total energy / energy per photon = 130 / 5.03 x 10^-19.

questions.topic: Effect of Higher Lamp PD on Frequency
questions.question: Explain the effect on the frequency of the UV light produced when the potential difference across the electrodes is increased.
questions.answer: Increasing the p.d. gives electrons more kinetic energy, so the emitted photons have higher energy and higher frequency.
steps: Greater p.d. gives electrons more kinetic energy (E = eV) before collisions.
Mercury atoms are excited to higher levels and emit photons with greater energy.
Since E = hf, the frequency of the UV light increases.

questions.question: Suggest why the hardening time is reduced when the UV lamp is moved closer to the screen.
questions.answer: Moving the lamp closer increases the intensity of UV light on the screen, so more energy arrives per second and the glue hardens faster.
steps: Intensity falls off with distance from the lamp (inverse square law).
Closer lamp means higher intensity at the screen.
More energy is delivered per second, so the same total energy is reached in a shorter time.

questions.question: One cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V is removed from an electric bicycle battery and connected to a 10 ohm variable resistor. The voltmeter reads 1.4 V. Calculate the internal resistance of the cell.
questions.answer: r = 0.71 ohm
steps: Lost volts = E - V = 1.5 - 1.4 = 0.1 V.
Current I = V / R = 1.4 / 10 = 0.14 A.
r = lost volts / I = 0.1 / 0.14 = 0.71 ohm.

questions.question: Explain why the battery gets hot when the e-bike goes up a steep hill.
questions.answer: Climbing a steep hill needs more power from the motor, so the battery supplies a larger current; the power wasted in its internal resistance (I^2 r) rises, and this is dissipated as heat.
steps: Going up a steep hill requires more work against gravity, so the motor needs more power.
The battery supplies more power, so the current drawn from it increases.
Power dissipated as heat in the battery's internal resistance is P = I^2 r.
Since I is larger, the power wasted as heat increases sharply, so the battery warms up.
